components.css: :host{--ink:#121212;--ink-2:#4A4A4A;--ink-3:#6B6B6B;--paper:#FFFFFF;--paper-2:#F4F4F1;--rule:#DCDCD7;--focus:#2860D8;--slab:'Zilla Slab',Rockwell,'Roboto Slab',Georgia,serif;--sans:'Libre Franklin','Franklin Gothic Medium','Helvetica Neue',Arial,sans-serif;--ease:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)}.ds-card{display:flex;flex-direction:column;width:260px;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);text-decoration:none;font-family:var(--sans);transition:border-color .2s,box-shadow .25s var(--ease)}.ds-card:hover{border-color:#B9B9B3;box-shadow:0 10px 24px -14px rgba(18,18,18,.35)}.ds-card:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:2px}.ds-band{display:grid;place-items:center;height:96px;background:var(--tile)}.ds-band svg{width:66px;height:66px;overflow:visible}.ds-body{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;padding:14px 18px 16px}.ds-name{font:700 23px/1.1 var(--slab)}.ds-line{color:var(--ink-2);font-size:15px;line-height:1.45}.ds-foot{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;margin-top:6px}.ds-today{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;font-size:13px;font-weight:700}.ds-today::before{content:'';width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--ink)}.ds-play{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;min-height:40px;padding:0 20px;border-radius:999px;background:var(--ink);color:#fff;font:600 14px/1 var(--sans)}.ds-mv{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference){.ds-card:hover .ds-mv,.ds-card:focus-visible .ds-mv{animation:ds-flip .9s var(--ease) 1}}@keyframes ds-flip{0%,100%{transform:scaleY(1)}45%,55%{transform:scaleY(.05)}}

narrative.overview:
BGameWorld reads like the day's puzzle page of a good newspaper: one calm, light sheet, dated at the top, where every game is a flat colour tile carrying its own drawn icon. "Today" is the headline. The date, the reset countdown and the Daily Seven sit above the games because the shared daily puzzle is the reason to come back. Everything else is paper, ink and hairline rules.

The density is a broadsheet's, not a dashboard's. Sections are separated by printed rules instead of boxes and backgrounds. Colour lives almost entirely in the game tiles, so the page's colour is the games themselves; the chrome around them stays black and white. Motion is held back to one signature: on hover or keyboard focus, a tile's icon performs a tiny version of its game's move, once, then rests.

The owner pinned the feel of the New York Times games hub, carried out entirely in BGameWorld's own materials: its own name, badge and logo, its own self-hosted faces (Zilla Slab and Libre Franklin, both SIL OFL), and its own authored icons. The dark neon game-portal template is rejected: no glows, gradient headlines, poster carousels or letter-spaced labels above headings.
keyCharacteristics: White paper ground, near-black ink, warm hairline grey rules.
One flat, light, saturated colour per game; ink icons sit on it.
Slab headlines and game names; a sturdy grotesque for everything else.
Black pill for the action, ink-outlined pill for the alternative.
Flat at rest; a soft lift on card hover and a shadow under the dialog are the only depth.
One tiny, game-specific icon move on hover or focus; nothing under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Colour Per Game Rule
rules.body: A tile colour belongs to exactly one game and appears only where that game appears. A new game gets a new flat colour, light enough that #121212 ink reads on it. Chrome, buttons and headings never borrow a tile colour.

rules.name: The Second Paper Rule
rules.body: #F4F4F1 is the only off-white. Use it for quieter sheets (footer, notes, boxed asides) and for hover fills on paper-coloured controls, never as the main page ground.

rules.name: The No Gloss Rule
rules.body: Every colour is flat: no gradients, glows or glass, on tiles or anywhere else.

rules.name: The Slab Names Things Rule
rules.body: Zilla Slab is for titles and names only: the page title, section heads, game names, the wordmark, leaderboard ranks, and letters drawn inside icons. Body, buttons, labels and navigation are always Libre Franklin.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels stay in sentence case at normal tracking. No uppercase, letter-spaced labels anywhere, and nothing set above a heading.

rules.name: The Two Rules Rule
rules.body: A 3px ink rule starts a new part of the edition: under the masthead, above the FAQ, above the dialog leaderboard, and under the "last updated" line on legal pages. A 1px hairline separates items within a part. Never use any other rule weight.

rules.name: The Flat By Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat. A shadow appears only as a response (card hover) or for a true overlay (the dialog).

rules.name: The One Move Rule
rules.body: An icon moves only in answer to hover or focus, performs its own game's move once, and stops. It never loops, never plays on load, and never moves under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Ink On Colour Rule
rules.body: Game art is always drawn in ink on its flat tile colour. Never use photos, painted posters, emoji or glyph characters as game tiles.

dos: **Do** give each game exactly one flat tile colour and draw its icon in #121212 on a 64-unit viewBox at a 2.5 stroke.
**Do** set titles and game names in Zilla Slab 700, and everything else in Libre Franklin, both self-hosted.
**Do** use a black pill (999px) for the single action in a band, and an ink-outlined pill for the alternative.
**Do** separate parts of the page with the 3px ink rule and items within a part with the 1px #DCDCD7 hairline.
**Do** use #F4F4F1 as the second paper for the footer, notes and hover fills.
**Do** keep every tap target at least 44px on phones, and keep the 3px #2860D8 focus outline on everything interactive.
**Do** keep the BGameWorld name, badge and logo, and the "-ezy" game names.
donts: **Don't** use the New York Times name, logo or "T" mark, or its licensed typefaces (Cheltenham, Karnak, NYT Franklin), and don't copy NYT game art, code, word lists or puzzles.
**Don't** use gradients, glows, glass, neon or dark portal grounds.
**Don't** put letter-spaced uppercase labels or any text above a heading.
**Don't** reuse a game's tile colour on chrome, buttons or another game.
**Don't** put the painted posters from `art/` back onto homepage tiles. They are for social only.
**Don't** loop icon motion, play it on load, or run it under reduced motion.
**Don't** add shadows to surfaces at rest.
